title: A Fourier term is bounded by stable influence
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $\rho\ge0$. For every subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and coordinate $i\in S$, the term $\rho^{|S|-1}\widehat f(S)^2$ is at most the stable influence $\sum_{T\ni i}\rho^{|T|-1}\widehat f(T)^2$, where $\widehat f(T)$ is the uniform Fourier coefficient of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
$S$ is a subset of the coordinates
